# P11 next-recorded-vote log loss, protocol fixed before new scores

Use the existing six-component mixture (unchanged estimator) on two author releases. MultiNLI matched development fits and mismatched development tests, following the previous Brier experiment on a known holdout. SNLI development fits and test evaluates on a fresh corpus. Fit each corpus separately. Retain all rows with five valid entailment/neutral/contradiction labels, including disputed rows. Exclude any evaluation row sharing prompt or normalized premise with a fitting row. Group by connected prompt/premise components (SNLI captionID, including full image grouping by prefix before '#'). Do not pool corpora. Use natural logarithms, nats per recorded vote. For each eligible row enumerate all five leave-one-vote-out targets. Weight recorded positions equally within each cohort. Model input consists solely of the other four categorical counts. ID, construction position, text and split metadata cannot enter the forecasts.

Report all votes (primary), unanimous visible four, and non-unanimous visible four, with the latter two secondary. Freeze these cuts independently of the held label. Preserve nulls and negative comparisons. Positive finding in a corpus/cohort requires lower confidence bound strictly above zero nats for EVERY baseline minus candidate difference there. Overall success requires this in BOTH primary cohorts; secondary analyses cannot rescue primary failure. Use 10,000 paired cluster bootstrap replicates per corpus, percentile intervals with Bonferroni family of 2 corpora x 3 cohorts x 6 baselines (36); intervals conditional on fitted forecasts. Report any undefined cell. Same draws for all methods and cohorts within a corpus.

Fit on all five-vote development histograms. Reuse mixture6, mixture3 and Dirichlet maximum-likelihood estimators from the original run. Compare against (1) empirical four-vote frequency shrunk towards uniform, tuning total pseudo-count over .001,.01,.1,.25,.5,1,2,4,8,16,32,64; (2) Jeffreys .5 per class; (3) Laplace 1 per class; (4) fitted Dirichlet; (5) three-class latent mixture; (6) saturated four-count conditional vote histogram shrunk to fitted Dirichlet with strength in .01,.1,1,5,25,125,625,3125. All distributions have full support. Tune (1) and (6) by minimum pooled held-vote log loss in five development folds defined by SHA-256(component) mod 5, refitting each prior on training folds. Smaller strength wins ties. Lock tables before reading test labels. No post-test tuning, corpus substitution, or claimed independent reviewer identity. Retain sufficient item counts, group identifiers, forecast tables, tuning traces, split audits, intervals and source hashes for replay.
